Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka will bat first in this Super Over, and we can see Kusal Perera padded up in the dugout. And it seems like Dasun Shanaka will walk to bat with him. The Indians have already taken the field again. Arshdeep Singh will bowl those crucial 6 balls for India. Here we go...

Still call it a dead rubber, aye? The Asia Cup has come alive right before the Finale. After 240 balls, we do not have a clear winner here. Sri Lanka bossed up almost 90 percent of the innings with the bat, but a few minor slip-ups on the way, nothing separates the teams. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST SUPER OVER OF ASIA CUP 2025! For the first time in this competition, the Indian bowling unit was put under pressure as they kept leaking runs in all phases. Hardik Pandya picked up the first wicket for India, but was off the field for the rest of the game due to a possible injury. Pathum Nissanka's maiden T20I century dented the Indian bowling unit badly and a decent hand from Kusal Perera also compounded their struggles. But it was that little patch in the middle overs when the Indian spinners bowled a few quiet overs, and also took a few important wickets as Sri Lanka slipped from 134/1 to 163/4. Pathum Nissanka, along with Dasun Shanaka kept the flame alive, but Arshdeep Singh delivered a fantastic penultimate over against two proper hitters, and with Nissanka getting out in the first delivery of the final over, Sri Lanka eventually could not cross the line despite flirting with a historic victory.

WE ARE IN FOR A SUPER OVER! Harshit Rana bowls this on a hard length, on middle, Dasun Shanaka gets hurried but manages to force it down to long on, where Axar Patel charges onto the ball but fails to pick up cleanly. However, Shanaka is only worried about getting the second run, he puts in a dive at the other end. Patel recovers and throws it at the bowler's end, where Harshit Rana also does not grab it on the first attempt, but no harm done. SRI LANKA ALSO ENDS ON 202/5!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.6: Harshit Rana to Dasun Shanaka, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Nerves! SKY, Gill, and Rana are in a conference, and a lot of field changes are being made. Three fielders are now in the deep in the leg side. Are we going into the Super Over?

FOUR! Streaky but Sri Lanka won't mind one bit! Pitched up and outside off, Dasun Shanaka throws his bat at it but gets an outside edge over short third man for a boundary. Still all three results are possible. Sri Lanka needs a four or a six to win, a double will force a Super Over, and anything less, India wins.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.5: Harshit Rana to Dasun Shanaka, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Sloppy again! Fuller one and on middle, Dasun Shanaka stays deep inside his crease and lofts it away towards deep mid-wicket, where Shivam Dube misfields and allows the second run. 7 needed in 2 now!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.4: Harshit Rana to Dasun Shanaka, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of pace from Rana, full and around off, Janith Liyanage goes through his slog way early and misses. The ball rolls towards the keeper, where Sanju Samson fumbles a bit, allowing a bye. 9 needed in 3 now
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.3: Harshit Rana to Janith Liyanage, Bye.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...SAFE! Hard length and around off, Janith Liyanage looks to pull but loses his bottom hand and gets a top edge. The ball flies towards the vacant mid off region. SKY from extra covers runs to his right, extending his right hand to catch, but fails to reach it. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.2: Harshit Rana to Janith Liyanage, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Janith Liyanage is in at 7. Sri Lanka need 12 off 5 balls now!

OUT! TAKEN! STRAIGHT TO THE FIELDER! Pathum Nissanka is shell-shocked at the crease, and so is Sanath Jayasuriya in the Lankan hut. Harshit Rana sees the batter move across but attacks the stumps, fuller in length. Pathum Nissanka tries to whip it away, but unfortunately hits it straight at short fine, where Varun Chakaravarthy shows good reflexes to grab it above his head. An inch either side and it would have been a boundary. Nissanka departs after a magnificent 107 off 58, and to a big applause from the crowd. Sri Lanka still need 12 runs in 5 balls!
Commentary.Howout: c Varun Chakaravarthy b Harshit Rana
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 19.1: Harshit Rana to Pathum Nissanka, OUT! c Varun Chakaravarthy b Harshit Rana.

Commentary.Commentary: Harshit Rana, who has been completely off the rhythm this evening, will bowl the final over. He has gone for 44 runs off his 3 overs. Can he defend 11 runs for his side? This is going all down to the wire, folks!

However, Rinku Singh is at mid on and the ball goes well over him. He chases after and puts in a dive, but fails to stop it from going to the fence.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 18.6: Arshdeep Singh to Dasun Shanaka, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Gets the wide yorker right this time, outside off, Dasun Shanaka throws his bat and squeezes it out towards deep backward point for just a run. 18 needed in 8 now. Sri Lanka needs a boundary in the next two balls.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 17.1: Axar Patel to Dasun Shanaka, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka still need 33 runs off the last 3 overs. Axar Patel (2-0-22-0) is back on.

SIX! BOOM! HUNDRED FOR NISSANKA! MAIDEN T20I HUNDRED FOR HIM! An innings from the top drawer, but he will want to finish the job for his country here. This is also the first century of this year's Asia Cup by any batter. Arshdeep Singh misses his mark and serves this full, on off, Pathum Nissanka gets underneath it and smokes it over the long off fence for a biggie. Nissanka raises his bat and helmet to take in all the applause, but now he will want to stay till the end to finish the job.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 16.6: Arshdeep Singh to Pathum Nissanka, Six!

Shanaka makes his ground.

The ball goes miles in the air towards deep square leg, where Axar Patel settles under it and takes an excellent catch. Sri Lanka 163/4 now, needing 40 in 20!

Kusal Perera comes dancing down the track and tries to work across, but the ball spins away from him and Sanju Samson does the rest with the southpaw out by a fair margin. Kusal Perera departs for an explosive 58 off just 32 and Sri Lanka are 134/2, needing another 69 runs off 46 balls.

Arshdeep Singh dives to his left and throws in a motion toward the batter's end, but misses his shy. Nissanka rushes inside the crease.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Sri Lanka have saved their best for the last. They have outplayed the Indians with the bat so far. At the same stage, India were 100/3 and Sri Lanka are 114/1. After bossing up the Powerplay, the bigger challenge for them was to deal with the in-form Indian spin attack. But they came out with flying colors against the spin trio. They have kept attacking on anything loose thrown at them and as a result, the pressure has shifted on the Indians. They are in a desperate search for wickets now as with 9 wickets in hand, this, right now, looks like an easily doable job for Sri Lanka. 89 needed off the last 10 overs. Here's Harshit Rana into the attack after the break. He replaces Kuldeep Yadav.
Much quicker, shortish and outside off, Pathum Nissanka slashes hard at it but fails to connect. 11 runs off the over, 25 in the last two!

Nissanka smoked that short ball towards long on where Axar Patel settled under it and tried to take it with a reverse cup. But the ball popped out of his palms and tipped behind the ropes. However, that won't count now as the umpire mentions that Abhishek Sharma had not gone off the field before the ball was delivered.

Flighted, full and around off, Pathum Nissanka looks to sweep it but hits it from the inner half of the bat towards mid-wicket. The fielder from the deep runs in to collect it but the batters pick up a couple of runs.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 8.6: Kuldeep Yadav to Kusal Perera, 1 run.
